import numpy as np, pandas as pd
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv')
tr['lgy']=np.log(tr.default_rate)
L={c:np.log(tr[c]) for c in ['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']}
segs=[(9,36,'q10-36'),(36,60,'q37-60'),(60,80,'q61-80'),(9,80,'ALL')]
for c in ['bbb_spread','sp500','nasdaq','vix','unemployment','gdp']:
    print(f"\n{c}: corr with log(sp500) / corr with lgy  by segment")
    for lo,hi,lab in segs:
        d=tr.iloc[lo:hi]
        m1=d[[c,'sp500']].notna().all(axis=1)
        m2=d[[c,'lgy']].notna().all(axis=1)
        r1=np.corrcoef(L[c][m1],L['sp500'][m1])[0,1] if m1.sum()>5 else np.nan
        r2=np.corrcoef(L[c][m2],d.lgy[m2])[0,1] if m2.sum()>5 else np.nan
        r3=np.corrcoef(L['sp500'][m2],d.lgy[m2])[0,1] if m2.sum()>5 else np.nan
        print(f"   {lab:8s} n={m2.sum():3d}  corr({c},sp500)={r1:+.3f}   corr({c},lgy)={r2:+.3f}   corr(sp500,lgy)={r3:+.3f}")
# partial correlation of lgy with log sp500 controlling for log bbb, per segment
import statsmodels.api as sm
print("\npartial corr(lgy, log sp500 | log bbb, unemp):")
for lo,hi,lab in segs:
    d=tr.iloc[lo:hi][['lgy','sp500','bbb_spread','unemployment']].dropna()
    if len(d)<8: print(f"   {lab}: too few"); continue
    X=sm.add_constant(d[['bbb_spread','unemployment']]); m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
    res=m.resid
    X2=sm.add_constant(d[['sp500']]); m2=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X2).fit()
    res2=m2.resid
    print(f"   {lab:8s} n={len(d):3d} partial_corr={np.corrcoef(res,res2)[0,1]:+.3f}")
EOF
```

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); tr['lgy']=np.log(tr.default_rate)
for c in ['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']:
    tr['L_'+c]=np.log(tr[c])
T=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)
segs=[(9,36,'q10-36'),(36,60,'q37-60'),(60,80,'q61-80'),(9,80,'ALL')]
specs=[('bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'),
       ('bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp'),
       ('bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','sp500'),
       ('unemployment','vix','gdp'),
       ('gdp','unemployment','vix'),
       ('unemployment','vix'),
       ('unemployment','gdp','vix','bbb_spread','sp500'),
       ('gdp','unemployment','vix','cpi','hpi'),
       ('bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'),
       ('bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp','cpi'),
       ]
for lo,hi,lab in segs:
    print(f"-- {lab}")
    for sp in specs:
        cols=[('L_'+c if c!='unemployment' else 'unemployment') for c in sp]
        d=T.iloc[lo:hi][['lgy']+cols].dropna()
        if len(d)<len(sp)+4: continue
        X=sm.add_constant(d[cols]); m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
        co=" ".join(f"{c}:{m.params.values[i+1]:+.2f}(t{m.tvalues.values[i+1]:+.1f})" for i,c in enumerate(sp))
        print(f"   n={len(d):3d} R2={m.rsquared:.3f} sd={np.std(m.resid):.3f} {co}")
EOF
python work/segments_clean2.py

cd /workspace && cat > work/constrained.py <<'EOF'
"""Can the data support the 'classic' credit-model signs (stress up -> defaults up,
   economy/equities up -> defaults down)?  If yes, the scenario truth would be
   materially higher than an unconstrained fit suggests."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy.optimize import lsq_linear
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
tr['src']='tr'; sc['src']='sc'; sc['default_rate']=np.nan
comb=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
comb['lgy']=np.log(comb.default_rate); comb['qf']=comb.quarter.astype(float)
T=comb[~comb.quarter.isin([37])].reset_index(drop=True)

def build(cols, d):
    X=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(d))]+[np.log(d[c]).values if c!='unemployment' else d[c].values for c in cols])
    return X
def constrained_fit(cols, lo, hi, d):
    X=build(cols,d); y=d.lgy.values
    res=lsq_linear(X,y,bounds=(lo,hi))
    resid=y-X@res.x
    return res.x, np.std(resid,ddof=len(cols)), 1-np.sum(resid**2)/np.sum((y-y.mean())**2)

cases=[
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],                [0,0,0],   [np.inf]*3, 'free'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],                [0,0,0],   [np.inf]*3, 'free'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp'],          [0,0,0,-np.inf],[np.inf]*4,'classic(gdp<=0)'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','sp500'],        [0,0,0,-np.inf],[np.inf]*4,'classic(sp500<=0)'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp','sp500'],  [0,0,0,-np.inf,-np.inf],[np.inf]*5,'classic(gdp&sp500<=0)'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'],                [0,0,-np.inf],[np.inf]*3,'classic(gdp<=0)'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','sp500'],              [0,0,-np.inf],[np.inf]*3,'classic(sp500<=0)'),
]
print(f"{'spec':58s}{'sd':>7s}{'R2':>7s}   coefficients (const last shown separately)")
for cols,lo,hi,tag in cases:
    need=list(cols)+['lgy']
    d=T.dropna(subset=need)
    x,sd,r2=constrained_fit(cols,lo,hi,d)
    co=" ".join(f"{c}:{v:+.2f}" for c,v in zip(cols,x[1:]))
    print(f"{tag+' '+str(cols):58s}{sd:7.3f}{r2:7.3f}   const={x[0]:+.2f}  {co}")
    # scenario prediction
    s=comb[comb.src=='sc']
    ds=s.dropna(subset=cols)
    Xs=build(cols,ds); pred=np.exp(Xs@x)
    print(f"{'':58s}   scenario: {pred[0]:.4f} -> {pred[-1]:.4f}")
EOF
python work/constrained.py
```

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy.optimize import lsq_linear
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
tr['src']='tr'; sc['src']='sc'; sc['default_rate']=np.nan
comb=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
comb['lgy']=np.log(comb.default_rate); comb['qf']=comb.quarter.astype(float)
T=comb[~comb.quarter.isin([37])].reset_index(drop=True)
INF=np.inf
def build(cols,d):
    return np.column_stack([np.ones(len(d))]+[ (np.log(d[c]).values if c!='unemployment' else d[c].values) for c in cols])
def fit(cols, lo, hi, d, free=False):
    X=build(cols,d); y=d.lgy.values
    if free:
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(X,y,rcond=None)[0]
    else:
        L=np.array([-INF]+list(lo),float); H=np.array([INF]+list(hi),float)
        b=lsq_linear(X,y,bounds=(L,H)).x
    resid=y-X@b
    return b, np.std(resid,ddof=len(cols)), 1-np.sum(resid**2)/np.sum((y-y.mean())**2)
cases=[
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],[0,0,0],[INF,INF,INF],'FREE'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp'],[0,0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC gdp<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','sp500'],[0,0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC sp500<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp','sp500'],[0,0,0,-INF,-INF],[INF,INF,INF,0,0],'CLASSIC gdp&sp500<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'],[0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC gdp<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','sp500'],[0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC sp500<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','hpi'],[0,0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC hpi<=0'),
 (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','cpi'],[0,0,0,-INF],[INF,INF,INF,0],'CLASSIC cpi<=0'),
]
for cols,lo,hi,tag in cases:
    d=T.dropna(subset=list(cols)+['lgy'])
    b,sd,r2=fit(cols,lo,hi,d,free=(tag=='FREE'))
    co=" ".join(f"{c}:{v:+.2f}" for c,v in zip(cols,b[1:]))
    s=comb[comb.src=='sc'].dropna(subset=cols)
    pred=np.exp(build(cols,s)@b)
    print(f"{tag:24s} n={len(d):3d} sd={sd:.3f} R2={r2:.3f} const={b[0]:+.2f} {co}")
    print(f"{'':24s} scenario: {pred[0]:.4f} -> {pred[-1]:.4f}   (rise x{pred[-1]/pred[0]:.2f})")

"""Does the 95% band hold up in the quarters whose macro configuration is most
   stress-like (the regime the scenario is in)?  If the model is systematically
   wrong there, the band must be widened."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
from ensemble import build
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); tr['lgy']=np.log(tr.default_rate); tr['qf']=tr.quarter.astype(float)
sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')

# stress score: bbb level, vix level, unemployment, falling gdp/equities (z-scores on training)
def stress_score(d, ref):
    z=lambda c: (np.log(d[c])-np.log(ref[c]).mean())/np.log(ref[c]).std()
    return (z('bbb_spread')+z('vix')+z('unemployment')-z('gdp')-z('sp500'))/5.0
ref=tr
tr['stress']=stress_score(tr,ref)
scn=sc.copy(); scn['stress']=stress_score(scn,ref)
print("scenario stress scores:", np.round(scn.stress.values,2))
print("training stress score: min %.2f  median %.2f  max %.2f"%(tr.stress.min(),tr.stress.median(),tr.stress.max()))
top=tr.nlargest(12,'stress')[['quarter','stress','default_rate']]
print("\nmost stress-like training quarters:"); print(top.to_string(index=False))

rows=[]
for t in range(30,81):
    train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
    if len(tgt)==0: continue
    try: o=build(train,tgt,exclude=(37,))
    except Exception: continue
    act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0]); yp=float(o['y_pred'][0])
    rows.append(dict(q=t,act=act,pred=yp,lo=float(o['y_lower'][0]),hi=float(o['y_upper'][0]),
                     sigma=float(o['sigma'][0]),stress=float(tr.loc[tr.quarter==t,'stress'].values[0])))
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
df['in']=(df.loo if False else df.lo<=df.act)&(df.act<=df.hi)
print("\nbacktest by stress decile:")
df['grp']=pd.qcut(df.stress,3,labels=['low','mid','high'])
for g,sub in df.groupby('grp',observed=True):
    print(f"  {g:5s} n={len(sub):2d} stress<={sub.stress.max():.2f}  MAE={np.mean(abs(sub.pred-sub.act)):.5f} "
          f"coverage={sub['in'].mean():.3f}  mean z={(np.log(sub.act)-np.log(sub.pred))/sub.sigma .mean():+.2f}"
          if False else
          f"  {g:5s} n={len(sub):2d} stress<={sub.stress.max():.2f}  MAE={np.mean(abs(sub.pred-sub.act)):.5f} "
          f"coverage={sub['in'].mean():.3f}  mean_z={np.mean((np.log(sub.act)-np.log(sub.pred))/sub.sigma):+.2f}")
hi=df[df.grp=='high']
print(f"\nhigh-stress quarters: {hi.q.tolist()}")
print(f"  coverage there: {hi['in'].mean():.3f}   MAE {np.mean(abs(hi.pred-hi.act)):.5f}")
print(f"  mean |z| = {np.mean(np.abs((np.log(hi.act)-np.log(hi.pred))/hi.sigma)):.2f}")
print(f"\noverall coverage {df['in'].mean():.3f}  MAE {np.mean(abs(df.pred-df.act)):.5f}")
EOF

"""Would adding / removing specifications improve the historical backtest?"""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
import ensemble as E

tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); tr['lgy']=np.log(tr.default_rate); tr['qf']=tr.quarter.astype(float)

def build_set(train_df, target_df, names, exclude=(37,)):
    fits=[]
    for spec in E.MODELS:
        if spec['name'] not in names: continue
        d=train_df[~train_df.quarter.isin(exclude)].dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['lgy'])
        if len(d)<20: continue
        if target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any(): continue
        X=E.design(d,spec); m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
        resid=np.asarray(m.resid); sd=float(np.std(resid,ddof=X.shape[1]))
        mse=float(resid@resid/max(len(d)-X.shape[1],1))
        cvm=E.cv_mae(d,spec,first_test=int(d.quarter.min())+20)
        Xs=E.design(target_df,spec)[X.columns]; p=np.asarray(m.predict(Xs))
        inv=np.linalg.pinv(X.values.T@X.values); lev=np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i',Xs.values,inv,Xs.values)
        fits.append(dict(sd=sd,cv=cvm,p=p,se=mse*np.sqrt(lev)))
    cvs=np.array([f['cv'] for f in fits]); w=np.exp(-(cvs-cvs.min())/0.0010); w=w/w.sum()
    P=np.array([f['p'] for f in fits]); S=np.array([f['se'] for f in fits])
    yp=(w[:,None]*np.exp(P)).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()
    vm=float(np.sum(w[:,None]*(np.exp(P)-yp[None,:])**2).sum()/(len(yp)*np.mean(yp)**2))
    sp=np.sqrt(np.sum(w[:,None]*S**2,axis=0))
    sig=1.10*np.sqrt(float(np.sum(w*np.array([f['sd'] for f in fits])))**2+float(np.mean(sp**2))+vm+0.05**2)
    return yp, yp*np.exp(-1.96*sig), yp*np.exp(1.96*sig)

BASE=[m['name'] for m in E.MODELS]
EXTRA=dict(name='bbb+unemp+vix+gdp', cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix','gdp'], log=('bbb_spread','vix','gdp'))
E.MODELS.append(EXTRA)
SETS={
 'BASE (8 models)': BASE,
 '+vix+gdp (9)': BASE+['bbb+unemp+vix+gdp'],
 'no-equity (6)': [n for n in BASE if n not in ('bbb+unemp+nasdaq','bbb+unemp+sp500')],
 'core5 (no trend)':[n for n in BASE if n!='bbb+unemp+trend'][:6],
 'stress-weighted':['bbb+unemp','bbb+unemp+vix','bbb+unemp+vix+gdp','bbb+unemp+gdp','bbb+unemp+cpi','bbb+unemp+hpi'],
}
for label,names in SETS.items():
    errs=[];cov=[];preds=[]
    for t in range(40,81):
        train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
        if len(tgt)==0: continue
        try: yp,lo,hi=build_set(train,tgt,names)
        except Exception: continue
        act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0])
        errs.append(abs(yp[0]-act)); cov.append(lo[0]<=act<=hi[0]); preds.append(yp[0])
    # scenario path
    sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv'); sc['qf']=sc.quarter.astype(float); sc['src']='sc'; sc['lgy']=np.nan
    tr2=tr.copy(); tr2['src']='tr'
    yp,lo,hi=build_set(tr2,sc,names)
    print(f"{label:18s} backtest MAE={np.mean(errs):.5f} RMSE={np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(errs))):.5f} cov={np.mean(cov):.3f} | scenario {yp[0]:.4f} -> {yp[-1]:.4f}  band q89 [{hi[-1]*0+lo[-1]:.4f},{hi[-1]:.4f}]")
EOF
python work/ensemble_sets.py
```

# Quarterly default-rate model — model report

**Deliverable:** `predictions.csv` (9 rows, one per scenario quarter 81–89).
**Script:** `build_predictions.py` (self-contained, reproducible from a fresh interpreter).

## 1. Specification

```
log(default_rate_t) = b0 + b1*log(bbb_spread_t) + b2*unemployment_t
                              + b3*(one further stress/level term)_t + eps_t
```

Forecasts are a **model average** over that family; intervals are built on the log scale.

## 2. Evidence behind each design choice

| Choice | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `log(bbb_spread)` is the core driver | elasticity 1.2–1.4, t>6 in *every* sub-sample; best of all single drivers; log form beats level/MA/lag forms (AIC 56.4 vs 55.0 with a far weaker t-stat; lagged (k=1..6) and trailing-MA (k=2..8) versions fit worse) |
| `unemployment` linear, small positive | t≈2–3 in multivariate fits; coefficient +0.05…+0.13 per pp |
| `vix` optional | strong predictor in the early window (t=+4.8) but redundant with the spread later; full-sample elasticity only +0.22 (t=1.3) → kept as an ensemble member, not as a core term |
| equity market / gdp / cpi / hpi / trend optional | 0.86–0.99 correlated with each other; no single one identifiable; the equity coefficient **flips sign** between sub-periods (nasdaq −1.10 in q1–40, +0.30 in q41–80) → a trend artefact, not a structural effect. They still add predictive power, so each is carried as an ensemble member rather than picked arbitrarily. |
| quarter 37 excluded | crisis-like macro row (unemp 13.6, VIX 54, spread 5.6) carrying the **lowest** default rate in the sample: 8–10σ from every stable specification; keeping it flattens the spread response and worsens the backtest MAE by 30% (0.0080 → 0.0105) |
| log link, multiplicative noise | default rate is positive and heteroskedastic in levels; log residuals are symmetric with sd≈0.34 |

**Model-form robustness.** Refitting with the *classic* credit signs forced (stress↑→defaults↑, GDP/equities↓→defaults↑) is statistically equivalent (sd 0.338–0.355 vs 0.349 free) — the answer does not depend on the sign assumptions.

**Guard against the "in-sample-only" trap.** The naive nine-series level fit has the best in-sample R² (0.57) but extrapolates to 0.045–0.15 default rates in the scenario. The model used here stays inside the historically observed default-rate range.

## 3. Validation (historical backtest, expanding window, 1-step-ahead, q40–80)

| variant | MAE | RMSE | 95% coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| **used** (exclude q37) | 0.0080 | 0.0109 | 92.7% → 100% after the 1.1 calibration |
| keep q37 | 0.0105 | 0.0141 | 87.8% |
| Huber (q37 down-weighted) | 0.0094 | 0.0127 | 92.7% |

High-stress-regime quarters only: coverage 94.1%, MAE 0.0102 → the model does **not** degrade in the scenario's regime. The scenario's composite stress score (−0.57…+0.63) lies inside the training range (−1.01…+2.28), so the forecast is interpolation in stress terms, not extrapolation.

## 4. Uncertainty

σ_log ≈ 0.40 = residual noise 0.34 ⊕ parameter uncertainty 0.04 ⊕ model disagreement 0.12 ⊕ out-of-support term 0.05, ×1.1 (backtest calibration) → 95% band ≈ point × [0.46, 2.18].

## 5. Sensitivity of the answer

| variation | y_pred q81 | y_pred q89 |
|---|---|---|
| **final** | 0.0339 | 0.0640 |
| Huber instead of dropping q37 | 0.0314 | 0.0489 |
| keep q37 | 0.0292 | 0.0333 |
| uniform / residual-sd weights | 0.0335 / 0.0341 | 0.0635 / 0.0647 |
| drop equity models / drop trend / add vix+gdp | 0.0324–0.0341 | 0.0608–0.0652 |

Every variant except "keep q37" lies in a tight band; the reported 95% interval contains all of them.

## 6. Forecast

| quarter | y_pred | y_lower | y_upper |
|---|---|---|---|
| 81 | 0.0339 | 0.0155 | 0.0739 |
| 82 | 0.0369 | 0.0169 | 0.0804 |
| 83 | 0.0401 | 0.0184 | 0.0874 |
| 84 | 0.0435 | 0.0199 | 0.0948 |
| 85 | 0.0470 | 0.0215 | 0.1027 |
| 86 | 0.0509 | 0.0233 | 0.1111 |
| 87 | 0.0550 | 0.0251 | 0.1202 |
| 88 | 0.0593 | 0.0271 | 0.1298 |
| 89 | 0.0640 | 0.0292 | 0.1402 |

Default rate rises 3.4% → 6.4% (×1.9) across the stress path, driven by the BBB spread (+43%), VIX (+96%) and unemployment (+2.4 pp).

## 7. Known risks

* If the quarter-37 row is in fact generated by the same process (rather than being an injected anomaly), the truth would be ≈0.033–0.049 rather than 0.064 — still inside the reported band.
* The dominant residual risk is the level factor (GDP/CPI/HPI/equity/trend) whose identity cannot be separated from the data; it moves the forecast *level* by ~±25% but the *rise* by much less.
* Noise in the underlying relation is ±30% (1σ) — irreducible at n=80.

I stress-tested the two judgement calls that drive the answer rather than just re-running the fit:

**1. Sensitivity analysis (12 variants).** The forecast is invariant to everything except the outlier decision:

| variation | y_pred q81 | y_pred q89 |
|---|---|---|
| **final** | 0.0339 | 0.0640 |
| drop equity models / drop trend / add vix+gdp | 0.0324–0.0341 | 0.0608–0.0652 |
| uniform vs. residual-sd weights | 0.0335 / 0.0341 | 0.0635 / 0.0647 |
| Huber instead of dropping q37 | 0.0314 | 0.0489 |
| keep q37 | 0.0292 | 0.0333 |

**2. A decisive test on quarter 37** (the crisis row with the *lowest* default rate). I probed 72 single-driver transformations to see if *any* stable specification makes q37 a normal observation: none does for a spread-driven model (8–10σ), but equity-driven ones reach only ~2.4σ. Cross-referencing that with the *sign instability* of the equity coefficient across sub-periods (−1.10 in q1–40, +0.30 in q41–80) settles it: the spread response is the stable structure, the equity relation is a trend artefact, and q37's target is foreign to the process. Backtest agrees (MAE 0.0080 vs 0.0105).

**3. Sign-robustness check.** Refitting with classic credit signs *forced* (stress↑→defaults↑, GDP/equities↓→defaults↑) is statistically equivalent (sd 0.338–0.355 vs 0.349 free) — the answer doesn't hinge on sign assumptions.

**4. Regime-specific interval validation.** In the high-stress quarters (the scenario's regime) coverage is 94.1% and MAE 0.0102 — the model doesn't degrade there. The scenario's composite stress score (−0.57…+0.63) actually sits *inside* the training range (−1.01…+2.28), so this is interpolation in stress terms, not blind extrapolation.

"""Marginalise over the outlier TREATMENT (drop q37 vs. down-weight it with a
   Huber M-estimator) instead of asserting one.  The treatment is the single
   largest source of model uncertainty, so it belongs inside the model average."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm

tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
tr['src']='tr'; sc['src']='sc'; sc['default_rate']=np.nan
comb=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
comb['lgy']=np.log(comb.default_rate); comb['qf']=comb.quarter.astype(float)

MODELS=[
 dict(name='bbb+unemp',        cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',)),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+vix',    cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],    log=('bbb_spread','vix')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+nasdaq', cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','nasdaq'], log=('bbb_spread','nasdaq')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+sp500',  cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','sp500'],  log=('bbb_spread','sp500')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+gdp',    cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'],    log=('bbb_spread','gdp')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+cpi',    cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','cpi'],    log=('bbb_spread','cpi')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+hpi',    cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment','hpi'],    log=('bbb_spread','hpi')),
 dict(name='bbb+unemp+trend',  cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',), trend=True),
]
def design(d,spec):
    X=pd.DataFrame(index=d.index)
    for c in spec['cols']: X[c]=np.log(d[c]) if c in spec['log'] else d[c]
    if spec.get('trend'): X['trend']=d['qf']
    X.insert(0,'const',1.0); return X

def fit_member(train_df, target_df, spec, treatment):
    """treatment: 'drop' (exclude q37) or 'huber' (keep it, Huber M-estimator)"""
    df=train_df.copy()
    if treatment=='drop': df=df[df.quarter!=37]
    d=df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['lgy'])
    if len(d)<20: return None
    if target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any(): return None
    X=design(d,spec)
    if treatment=='huber':
        m=sm.RLM(d.lgy.values,X,M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit()
        w=np.asarray(m.model.weights)                     # robust weights
        resid=np.asarray(m.resid)
        scale=float(np.sqrt(np.sum(w*resid**2)/np.sum(w)))   # reweighted (robust) scale
        dfree=max(len(d)-X.shape[1],1)
        mse=float(np.sum(w*resid**2)/np.sum(w)/dfree)
    else:
        m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
        resid=np.asarray(m.resid); scale=float(np.std(resid,ddof=X.shape[1]))
        mse=float(resid@resid/max(len(d)-X.shape[1],1))
    Xs=design(target_df,spec)[X.columns]; p=np.asarray(m.predict(Xs))
    inv=np.linalg.pinv(X.values.T@X.values); lev=np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i',Xs.values,inv,Xs.values)
    return dict(spec=spec,treatment=treatment,m=m,d=d,X=X,sd=scale,se=mse*np.sqrt(lev),p=p,n=len(d))

def cv_score(train_df, spec, treatment, first_test=20, h=4):
    df=train_df.copy()
    if treatment=='drop': df=df[df.quarter!=37]
    d=df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['lgy'])
    if len(d)<first_test+10: return np.nan
    errs=[]
    for t in range(int(d.quarter.min())+first_test, int(d.quarter.max())-h+1):
        trn=d[d.quarter<t]; tst=d[(d.quarter>=t)&(d.quarter<t+h)]
        if len(trn)<15 or len(tst)==0: continue
        Xtr=design(trn,spec); Xte=design(tst,spec)[Xtr.columns]
        if treatment=='huber':
            mm=sm.RLM(trn.lgy.values,Xtr,M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit(); pr=mm.predict(Xte)
        else:
            b=np.linalg.lstsq(Xtr.values,trn.lgy.values,rcond=None)[0]; pr=Xte.values@b
        errs.extend(np.abs(np.exp(pr)-np.exp(tst.lgy.values)))
    return float(np.mean(errs)) if len(errs) else np.nan

def forecast(train_df, target_df, treatments=('drop','huber'), tau=0.0010, extra=0.05, calib=1.10):
    mem=[];cvs=[]
    for t in treatments:
        for spec in MODELS:
            f=fit_member(train_df,target_df,spec,t)
            if f is None: continue
            mem.append(f); cvs.append(cv_score(train_df,spec,t))
    cvs=np.array(cvs); ok=np.isfinite(cvs)
    w=np.where(ok,np.exp(-np.where(ok,cvs,0)-np.nanmin(cvs[ok]))/tau,1.0)
    w=np.where(ok,w,1.0/np.sum(ok)); w=w/w.sum()
    P=np.array([f['p'] for f in mem]); S=np.array([f['se'] for f in mem]); SD=np.array([f['sd'] for f in mem])
    yp=(w[:,None]*np.exp(P)).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()
    vm=float(np.sum(w[:,None]*(np.exp(P)-yp[None,:])**2).sum()/(len(yp)*np.mean(yp)**2))
    sp=np.sqrt(np.sum(w[:,None]*S**2,axis=0))
    sig=calib*np.sqrt(float(np.sum(w*SD))**2+float(np.mean(sp**2))+vm+extra**2)
    return dict(yp=yp,lo=yp*np.exp(-1.96*sig),hi=yp*np.exp(1.96*sig),sig=sig,w=w,mem=mem,cvs=cvs,
                sd_resid=float(np.sum(w*SD)),vm=vm,se_par=float(np.mean(sp)))

if __name__=='__main__':
    scn=comb[comb.src=='sc'].copy(); trn=comb[comb.src=='tr'].copy()
    for treat in [('drop',),('huber',),('drop','huber')]:
        o=forecast(trn,scn,treatments=treat)
        print(f"treatments={treat}: q81 {o['yp'][0]:.4f} -> q89 {o['yp'][-1]:.4f} | "
              f"sd_resid {o['sd_resid']:.3f} model_sd {np.sqrt(o['vm']):.3f} sigma {o['sig'].mean():.3f} "
              f"| q89 band [{o['lo'][-1]:.4f},{o['hi'][-1]:.4f}]")
    o=forecast(trn,scn,treatments=('drop','huber'))
    print("\nmembers and weights:")
    for f,wi,c in zip(o['mem'],o['w'],o['cvs']):
        print(f"  {f['treatment']:6s} {f['spec']['name']:22s} w={wi:.3f} cv={c:.5f} n={f['n']:3d} "
              f"y {np.exp(f['p'][0]):.4f}->{np.exp(f['p'][-1]):.4f} sd={f['sd']:.3f}")
EOF
python work/marginalise.py
```

cd /workspace && cat > build_predictions.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Quarterly portfolio default-rate model  ->  predictions.csv
=============================================================================

Data
----
data/train.csv    80 quarterly observations: 9 macro series + default_rate (fraction)
data/scenario.csv  9 forward quarters (81..89) under a forward stress scenario (no target)

Model
-----
    log(default_rate_t) = b0 + b1*log(bbb_spread_t) + b2*unemployment_t
                                  + b3*(one further stress/level term)_t + eps_t

The forecast is a MODEL AVERAGE over 8 specifications x 2 outlier treatments
(16 members), with weights set by expanding-window cross-validation.

Why this specification (all evidence from data/train.csv):
  * log(bbb_spread) is by far the strongest and most stable driver - elasticity
    ~1.2-1.4 with t>6 in every sub-sample, and it enters as a LOG rather than as a
    raw level (the "transformation" the task refers to).  One-quarter lags,
    trailing moving averages and a level (semi-log) form all fit worse.
  * unemployment enters linearly with a small positive coefficient.
  * the remaining series (gdp, hpi, sp500, djia, nasdaq, vix, cpi) are 0.86-0.99
    correlated with each other, so none can be identified on its own; each adds a
    little predictive power but none is stable across sub-periods (the equity
    coefficient flips sign between q1-40 and q41-80).  They are therefore carried
    as separate ensemble members rather than one being picked arbitrarily - this
    also avoids the multicollinearity explosion of the naive "all nine series in
    levels" fit, whose in-sample R^2 is the best but whose scenario extrapolation
    implies a 0.15 default rate (exactly the failure mode the task warns about).
  * quarter 37 (a crisis-like macro row) carries the LOWEST default rate of the
    whole sample: an outlier w.r.t. every economically sensible specification
    (>8 sigma).  Its treatment is the single largest modelling judgement in this
    analysis, so it is MARGINALISED OVER rather than asserted: half the ensemble
    drops it, half keeps it with a Huber M-estimator that down-weights it.  Both
    treatments are inside the reported 95% band.
  * the forecast is sign-robust: refitting with the classic credit signs forced
    (stress up -> defaults up, GDP/equities up -> defaults down) is
    statistically equivalent (sd 0.338-0.355 vs 0.349 free).

Uncertainty
-----------
95% prediction intervals are built on the log scale from
  (a) residual noise of the relation, (b) parameter (estimation) uncertainty,
  (c) model uncertainty (disagreement across the 16 averaged members),
  (d) an extra term because the scenario's joint configuration lies outside the
      training support,
and are finally scaled by 1.1, the factor that lifts the historical backtest
coverage of the nominal 95% band to ~100% (92.7% -> 100%).
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm

TRAIN, SCEN, OUT = 'data/train.csv', 'data/scenario.csv', 'predictions.csv'
OUTLIER_QUARTER = 37        # macro crisis row whose default rate is inconsistent
Z = 1.959963985             # normal 95% quantile
CALIB = 1.10                # backtest-calibrated widening of the nominal 95% band
TAU = 0.0010                # softmax temperature on the CV error
EXTRA = 0.05                # scenario lies outside the joint training support

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ load data
tr = pd.read_csv(TRAIN); sc = pd.read_csv(SCEN)
tr['src'] = 'tr'; sc['src'] = 'sc'; sc['default_rate'] = np.nan
comb = pd.concat([tr, sc], ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
comb['lgy'] = np.log(comb.default_rate)
comb['qf'] = comb.quarter.astype(float)
TRAIN_DF = comb[comb.src == 'tr'].copy()
SCEN_DF = comb[comb.src == 'sc'].copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------- candidate specifications
MODELS = [
    dict(name='bbb+unemp',        cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',)),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+vix',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'vix'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'vix')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+nasdaq', cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'nasdaq'], log=('bbb_spread', 'nasdaq')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+sp500',  cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'sp500'],  log=('bbb_spread', 'sp500')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+gdp',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'gdp'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'gdp')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+cpi',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'cpi'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'cpi')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+hpi',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'hpi'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'hpi')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+trend',  cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',), trend=True),
]
TREATMENTS = ['drop', 'huber']      # how the quarter-37 anomaly is handled

def design(d, spec):
    X = pd.DataFrame(index=d.index)
    for c in spec['cols']:
        X[c] = np.log(d[c]) if c in spec['log'] else d[c]
    if spec.get('trend', False):
        X['trend'] = d['qf']
    X.insert(0, 'const', 1.0)
    return X

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ one member
def fit_member(train_df, target_df, spec, treatment):
    """fit one (specification, outlier-treatment) member and forecast the targets"""
    df = train_df.copy()
    if treatment == 'drop':
        df = df[df.quarter != OUTLIER_QUARTER]
    d = df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols']) + ['lgy'])
    if len(d) < 20 or target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any():
        return None
    X = design(d, spec)
    if treatment == 'huber':                       # keep the row, down-weight it
        m = sm.RLM(d.lgy.values, X, M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit()
        wgt = np.asarray(m.model.weights)
        resid = np.asarray(m.resid)
        sd = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(wgt * resid ** 2) / np.sum(wgt)))          # robust scale
        dfree = max(len(d) - X.shape[1], 1)
        mse = float(np.sum(wgt * resid ** 2) / np.sum(wgt) / dfree)
        XtWX = X.values.T @ (wgt[:, None] * X.values)
    else:
        m = sm.OLS(d.lgy.values, X).fit()
        resid = np.asarray(m.resid)
        sd = float(np.std(resid, ddof=X.shape[1]))
        mse = float(resid @ resid / max(len(d) - X.shape[1], 1))
        XtWX = X.values.T @ X.values
    Xs = design(target_df, spec)[X.columns]
    p = np.asarray(m.predict(Xs))                                         # log forecast
    inv = np.linalg.pinv(XtWX)
    lev = np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i', Xs.values, inv, Xs.values)
    se = mse * np.sqrt(lev)                                               # parameter sd
    return dict(spec=spec, treatment=treatment, m=m, d=d, X=X, sd=sd, se=se, p=p, n=len(d))

def cv_score(train_df, spec, treatment, first_test=20, h=4):
    """expanding-window CV error of the member inside the training window"""
    df = train_df.copy()
    if treatment == 'drop':
        df = df[df.quarter != OUTLIER_QUARTER]
    d = df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols']) + ['lgy'])
    if len(d) < first_test + 10:
        return np.nan
    errs = []
    for t in range(int(d.quarter.min()) + first_test, int(d.quarter.max()) - h + 1):
        trn = d[d.quarter < t]; tst = d[(d.quarter >= t) & (d.quarter < t + h)]
        if len(trn) < 15 or len(tst) == 0:
            continue
        Xtr = design(trn, spec); Xte = design(tst, spec)[Xtr.columns]
        if treatment == 'huber':
            mm = sm.RLM(trn.lgy.values, Xtr, M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit()
            pr = mm.predict(Xte)
        else:
            b = np.linalg.lstsq(Xtr.values, trn.lgy.values, rcond=None)[0]
            pr = Xte.values @ b
        errs.extend(np.abs(np.exp(pr) - np.exp(tst.lgy.values)))
    return float(np.mean(errs)) if len(errs) else np.nan

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ build forecast
members, cvs = [], []
for treatment in TREATMENTS:
    for spec in MODELS:
        f = fit_member(TRAIN_DF, SCEN_DF, spec, treatment)
        if f is None:
            continue
        f['cv'] = cv_score(TRAIN_DF, spec, treatment)
        members.append(f); cvs.append(f['cv'])
cvs = np.array(cvs, dtype=float)
ok = np.isfinite(cvs)
expo = np.where(ok, -(cvs - np.nanmin(cvs[ok])) / TAU, 0.0)
w = np.exp(expo); w = w / w.sum()

P = np.array([f['p'] for f in members])       # (n_members, n_scen) log forecasts
S = np.array([f['se'] for f in members])      # parameter sd, log scale
SD = np.array([f['sd'] for f in members])     # residual scale, log scale
LVL = np.exp(P)

y_pred = (w[:, None] * LVL).sum(axis=0)       # model average on the level scale

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ uncertainty
sd_resid = float(np.sum(w * SD))
var_model = float(np.sum(w[:, None] * (LVL - y_pred[None, :]) ** 2).sum()
                     / (len(y_pred) * np.mean(y_pred) ** 2))
se_par = np.sqrt(np.sum(w[:, None] * S ** 2, axis=0))
sigma = CALIB * np.sqrt(sd_resid ** 2 + se_par ** 2 + var_model + EXTRA ** 2)

y_lower = y_pred * np.exp(-Z * sigma)
y_upper = y_pred * np.exp(+Z * sigma)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ write output
out = pd.DataFrame({
    'quarter': SCEN_DF['quarter'].values,
    'y_pred':  y_pred,
    'y_lower': y_lower,
    'y_upper': y_upper,
})
assert len(out) == len(SCEN_DF) == len(sc)
assert out.quarter.tolist() == sc.quarter.tolist()
assert np.isfinite(out[['y_pred', 'y_lower', 'y_upper']].values).all()

cd /workspace && cat > build_predictions.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Quarterly portfolio default-rate model  ->  predictions.csv
=============================================================================

Data
----
data/train.csv    80 quarterly observations: 9 macro series + default_rate (fraction)
data/scenario.csv  9 forward quarters (81..89) under a forward stress scenario (no target)

Model
-----
    log(default_rate_t) = b0 + b1*log(bbb_spread_t) + b2*unemployment_t
                                  + b3*(one further stress/level term)_t + eps_t

The forecast is a MODEL AVERAGE over 8 specifications x 2 outlier treatments
(16 members), with weights set by expanding-window cross-validation.

Why this specification (all evidence from data/train.csv):
  * log(bbb_spread) is by far the strongest and most stable driver - elasticity
    ~1.2-1.4 with t>6 in every sub-sample, and it enters as a LOG rather than as a
    raw level (the "transformation" the task refers to).  One-quarter lags,
    trailing moving averages and a level (semi-log) form all fit worse.
  * unemployment enters linearly with a small positive coefficient.
  * the remaining series (gdp, hpi, sp500, djia, nasdaq, vix, cpi) are 0.86-0.99
    correlated with each other, so none can be identified on its own; each adds a
    little predictive power but none is stable across sub-periods (the equity
    coefficient flips sign between q1-40 and q41-80).  They are therefore carried
    as separate ensemble members rather than one being picked arbitrarily - this
    also avoids the multicollinearity explosion of the naive "all nine series in
    levels" fit, whose in-sample R^2 is the best but whose scenario extrapolation
    implies a 0.15 default rate (exactly the failure mode the task warns about).
  * quarter 37 (a crisis-like macro row) carries the LOWEST default rate of the
    whole sample: an outlier w.r.t. every economically sensible specification
    (>8 sigma).  Its treatment is the single largest modelling judgement in this
    analysis, so it is MARGINALISED OVER rather than asserted: part of the
    ensemble drops it, part keeps it with a Huber M-estimator that down-weights
    it.  Both treatments sit inside the reported 95% band.
  * the forecast is sign-robust: refitting with the classic credit signs forced
    (stress up -> defaults up, GDP/equities up -> defaults down) is statistically
    equivalent (sd 0.338-0.355 vs 0.349 free).

Uncertainty
-----------
95% prediction intervals are built on the log scale from
  (a) residual noise of the relation, (b) parameter (estimation) uncertainty,
  (c) model uncertainty (disagreement across the 16 averaged members),
  (d) an extra term because the scenario's joint configuration lies outside the
      training support,
and are finally scaled by 1.1, the factor that lifts the historical backtest
coverage of the nominal 95% band to ~100% (92.7% -> 100%).
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

TRAIN, SCEN, OUT = 'data/train.csv', 'data/scenario.csv', 'predictions.csv'
OUTLIER_QUARTER = 37        # macro crisis row whose default rate is inconsistent
Z = 1.959963985             # normal 95% quantile
CALIB = 1.10                # backtest-calibrated widening of the nominal 95% band
TAU = 0.0010                # softmax temperature on the CV error
EXTRA = 0.05                # scenario lies outside the joint training support

# ------------------------------------------------------- candidate specifications
MODELS = [
    dict(name='bbb+unemp',        cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',)),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+vix',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'vix'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'vix')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+nasdaq', cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'nasdaq'], log=('bbb_spread', 'nasdaq')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+sp500',  cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'sp500'],  log=('bbb_spread', 'sp500')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+gdp',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'gdp'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'gdp')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+cpi',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'cpi'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'cpi')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+hpi',    cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment', 'hpi'],    log=('bbb_spread', 'hpi')),
    dict(name='bbb+unemp+trend',  cols=['bbb_spread', 'unemployment'],          log=('bbb_spread',), trend=True),
]
TREATMENTS = ['drop', 'huber']      # how the quarter-37 anomaly is handled


def design(d, spec):
    X = pd.DataFrame(index=d.index)
    for c in spec['cols']:
        X[c] = np.log(d[c]) if c in spec['log'] else d[c]
    if spec.get('trend', False):
        X['trend'] = d['qf']
    X.insert(0, 'const', 1.0)
    return X


def fit_member(train_df, target_df, spec, treatment):
    """fit one (specification, outlier-treatment) member and forecast target_df"""
    df = train_df.copy()
    if treatment == 'drop':
        df = df[df.quarter != OUTLIER_QUARTER]
    d = df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols']) + ['lgy'])
    if len(d) < 20 or target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any():
        return None
    X = design(d, spec)
    if treatment == 'huber':                       # keep the row, down-weight it
        m = sm.RLM(d.lgy.values, X, M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit()
        wgt = np.asarray(m.model.weights)
        resid = np.asarray(m.resid)
        sd = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(wgt * resid ** 2) / np.sum(wgt)))          # robust scale
        dfree = max(len(d) - X.shape[1], 1)
        mse = float(np.sum(wgt * resid ** 2) / np.sum(wgt) / dfree)
        XtWX = X.values.T @ (wgt[:, None] * X.values)
    else:
        m = sm.OLS(d.lgy.values, X).fit()
        resid = np.asarray(m.resid)
        sd = float(np.std(resid, ddof=X.shape[1]))
        mse = float(resid @ resid / max(len(d) - X.shape[1], 1))
        XtWX = X.values.T @ X.values
    Xs = design(target_df, spec)[X.columns]
    p = np.asarray(m.predict(Xs))                                         # log forecast
    inv = np.linalg.pinv(XtWX)
    lev = np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i', Xs.values, inv, Xs.values)
    se = mse * np.sqrt(lev)                                               # parameter sd
    return dict(spec=spec, treatment=treatment, m=m, d=d, X=X, sd=sd, se=se, p=p, n=len(d))


def cv_score(train_df, spec, treatment, first_test=20, h=4):
    """expanding-window CV error of the member inside the training window"""
    df = train_df.copy()
    if treatment == 'drop':
        df = df[df.quarter != OUTLIER_QUARTER]
    d = df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols']) + ['lgy'])
    if len(d) < first_test + 10:
        return np.nan
    errs = []
    for t in range(int(d.quarter.min()) + first_test, int(d.quarter.max()) - h + 1):
        trn = d[d.quarter < t]
        tst = d[(d.quarter >= t) & (d.quarter < t + h)]
        if len(trn) < 15 or len(tst) == 0:
            continue
        Xtr = design(trn, spec)
        Xte = design(tst, spec)[Xtr.columns]
        if treatment == 'huber':
            mm = sm.RLM(trn.lgy.values, Xtr, M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit()
            pr = mm.predict(Xte)
        else:
            b = np.linalg.lstsq(Xtr.values, trn.lgy.values, rcond=None)[0]
            pr = Xte.values @ b
        errs.extend(np.abs(np.exp(pr) - np.exp(tst.lgy.values)))
    return float(np.mean(errs)) if len(errs) else np.nan


def run_forecast(train_df, target_df, treatments=None, tau=TAU, extra=EXTRA, calib=CALIB):
    """Fit every (specification, treatment) member on train_df and forecast target_df."""
    treatments = treatments or TREATMENTS
    members = []
    for treatment in treatments:
        for spec in MODELS:
            f = fit_member(train_df, target_df, spec, treatment)
            if f is None:
                continue
            f['cv'] = cv_score(train_df, spec, treatment)
            members.append(f)
    cvs = np.array([f['cv'] for f in members], dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(cvs)
    expo = np.where(ok, -(cvs - np.nanmin(cvs[ok])) / tau, 0.0)
    w = np.exp(expo)
    w = w / w.sum()

    P = np.array([f['p'] for f in members])       # (n_members, n_target) log forecasts
    S = np.array([f['se'] for f in members])      # parameter sd, log scale
    SD = np.array([f['sd'] for f in members])     # residual scale, log scale
    LVL = np.exp(P)
    y_pred = (w[:, None] * LVL).sum(axis=0)       # model average on the level scale

    sd_resid = float(np.sum(w * SD))
    var_model = float(np.sum(w[:, None] * (LVL - y_pred[None, :]) ** 2).sum()
                         / (len(y_pred) * np.mean(y_pred) ** 2))
    se_par = np.sqrt(np.sum(w[:, None] * S ** 2, axis=0))
    sigma = calib * np.sqrt(sd_resid ** 2 + se_par ** 2 + var_model + extra ** 2)
    return dict(members=members, w=w, cvs=cvs, y_pred=y_pred,
                y_lower=y_pred * np.exp(-Z * sigma), y_upper=y_pred * np.exp(+Z * sigma),
                sigma=sigma, sd_resid=sd_resid, var_model=var_model, se_par=se_par)


def load_data():
    tr = pd.read_csv(TRAIN)
    sc = pd.read_csv(SCEN)
    tr['src'] = 'tr'
    sc['src'] = 'sc'
    sc['default_rate'] = np.nan
    comb = pd.concat([tr, sc], ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
    comb['lgy'] = np.log(comb.default_rate)
    comb['qf'] = comb.quarter.astype(float)
    return comb, comb[comb.src == 'tr'].copy(), comb[comb.src == 'sc'].copy(), sc


def main():
    comb, train_df, scen_df, sc = load_data()
    res = run_forecast(train_df, scen_df)
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        'quarter': scen_df['quarter'].values,
        'y_pred':  res['y_pred'],
        'y_lower': res['y_lower'],
        'y_upper': res['y_upper'],
    })
    assert len(out) == len(scen_df) == len(sc)
    assert out.quarter.tolist() == sc.quarter.tolist()
    assert np.isfinite(out[['y_pred', 'y_lower', 'y_upper']].values).all()
    assert (out.y_lower < out.y_pred).all() and (out.y_pred < out.y_upper).all()
    out.to_csv(OUT, index=False)

    print('=' * 92)
    print('model average: %d specifications x %d outlier treatments, weights from CV error'
          % (len(MODELS), len(TREATMENTS)))
    for f, wi in zip(res['members'], res['w']):
        co = ' '.join('%s=%+.3f' % (k, v) for k, v in zip(f['X'].columns[1:], f['m'].params.values[1:]))
        rr = np.asarray(f['m'].resid)
        yy = f['d'].lgy.values
        if f['treatment'] == 'huber':
            ww = np.asarray(f['m'].model.weights)
            ybar = np.sum(ww * yy) / np.sum(ww)
            r2 = 1 - np.sum(ww * rr ** 2) / np.sum(ww * (yy - ybar) ** 2)
        else:
            r2 = 1 - np.sum(rr ** 2) / np.sum((yy - yy.mean()) ** 2)
        print('  %-6s %-22s w=%.3f cvMAE=%.5f n=%3d R2=%.3f  %s'
              % (f['treatment'], f['spec']['name'], wi, f['cv'], f['n'], r2, co))
    print('\nresidual sd (log) %.3f | parameter sd (log) %.3f | model-spread sd (log) %.3f '
          '| out-of-support %.3f' % (res['sd_resid'], np.mean(res['se_par']),
                                     np.sqrt(res['var_model']), EXTRA))
    print('total sigma (log) %.3f -> 95%% band = point x [%.2f, %.2f]'
          % (res['sigma'].mean(), np.exp(-Z * res['sigma'].mean()), np.exp(Z * res['sigma'].mean())))
    print('\n' + out.to_string(index=False))
    print('=' * 92)
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Quarterly default-rate model — model report

**Deliverable:** `predictions.csv` (9 rows, one per scenario quarter 81–89).
**Script:** `build_predictions.py` — self-contained, deterministic, re-runnable from a fresh interpreter
(the same functions are used by the validation script, so the backtest exercises the production code path).

## 1. Specification

```
log(default_rate_t) = b0 + b1*log(bbb_spread_t) + b2*unemployment_t
                              + b3*(one further stress/level term)_t + eps_t
```

The forecast is a **model average over 8 specifications × 2 outlier treatments (16 members)**,
weighted by expanding-window CV error inside the training window.

| member | q81 | q89 |
|---|---|---|
| bbb+unemp | 0.0278 | 0.0520 |
| bbb+unemp+vix | 0.0276 | 0.0603 |
| bbb+unemp+nasdaq | 0.0317 | 0.0515 |
| bbb+unemp+sp500 | 0.0351 | 0.0740 |
| bbb+unemp+gdp | 0.0364 | 0.0651 |
| bbb+unemp+cpi | 0.0349 | 0.0641 |
| bbb+unemp+hpi | 0.0382 | 0.0652 |
| bbb+unemp+trend | 0.0363 | 0.0757 |

## 2. Evidence behind each design choice

| Choice | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `log(bbb_spread)` is the core driver | elasticity 1.2–1.4, t>6 in *every* sub-sample; best of all single drivers; the log form beats level / trailing-MA / lag forms (lag k=1..6 and MA k=2..8 all fit worse) |
| `unemployment` linear, small positive | t≈2–3 in multivariate fits; coefficient +0.05…+0.13 per pp |
| `vix` optional | strongest predictor in the early window (t=+4.8) but redundant with the spread later; full-sample elasticity only +0.22 (t=1.3) → ensemble member, not a core term |
| equity / gdp / cpi / hpi / trend optional | 0.86–0.99 correlated with each other; none identifiable alone; the equity coefficient **flips sign** between sub-periods (nasdaq −1.10 in q1–40, +0.30 in q41–80) → trend artefact, not structural. Carried as separate members rather than one being picked arbitrarily |
| quarter 37 marginalised, not asserted | crisis-like macro row (unemp 13.6, VIX 54, spread 5.6) with the **lowest** default rate in the sample: 8–10σ from every stable specification. Part of the ensemble drops it, part keeps it under a Huber M-estimator. Both outcomes (0.0640 / 0.0498 at q89) lie inside the reported band |
| log link, multiplicative noise | default rate is positive and heteroskedastic in levels; log residuals symmetric, sd ≈ 0.34 |

**Sign robustness.** Refitting with the *classic* credit signs forced (stress↑→defaults↑, GDP/equities↑→defaults↓) is statistically equivalent (sd 0.338–0.355 vs 0.349 free) — the answer does not depend on sign assumptions.

**Guard against the "in-sample-only" trap.** The naive nine-series level fit has the best in-sample R² (0.57) but extrapolates to 0.045–0.15 default rates in the scenario. The model used here stays inside the historically observed default-rate range.

## 3. Validation — expanding-window backtest, 1-step-ahead (production `run_forecast`)

| **final (marginalised)** | **0.00801** | **0.01092** | **97.6%** |
| drop q37 only | 0.00801 | 0.01091 | 97.5% |
| Huber q37 only | 0.00924 | 0.01259 | 87.8% |

## What this step added

I resolved the one decision the sensitivity analysis flagged as dominant — **how to treat the quarter-37 anomaly**, which swings the q89 forecast between 0.033 and 0.064 — by **marginalising over it instead of asserting one treatment**:

- The ensemble now has 16 members: 8 specifications × 2 outlier treatments (drop q37 / keep it with a Huber M-estimator that down-weights it). CV evidence gives the "drop" family ~94% of the weight, so the point estimate barely moves (0.0640 → 0.0630), but the treatment uncertainty now lives *inside* the reported band instead of outside it. Both treatments' answers (0.0640 and 0.0498 at q89) are verified to sit inside the final interval.

Along the way I found and fixed a real bug in my prototype: the softmax temperature was being applied *after* `exp` rather than inside it, which had silently flattened the CV weights to uniform. Correcting it restored the intended weighting (and changed the marginalised point estimate from 0.0570 to 0.0630 — worth catching before it shipped).

I also refactored `build_predictions.py` so the forecast is a callable function, meaning the validation script now exercises the **exact production code path** rather than a look-alike.

"""Independent model-class check: does a non-parametric learner (gradient boosting /
   random forest) corroborate the log-linear, spread-driven structure, and what does
   it say about the scenario?  This is a structural check, not a replacement model."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor, RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV
import statsmodels.api as sm

tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
tr['src']='tr'; sc['src']='sc'; sc['default_rate']=np.nan
comb=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True).reset_index(drop=True)
comb['lgy']=np.log(comb.default_rate)
DR=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']

def feats(d):
    F={}
    for c in DR:
        v=d[c]; F[c]=v; F['log_'+c]=np.log(v.where(v>0))
    return pd.DataFrame(F,index=d.index)

X=feats(comb); trn=comb[comb.src=='tr'].copy(); scn=comb[comb.src=='sc'].copy()
trn=trn[trn.quarter!=37]           # outlier row excluded (consistent with the main model)
ntr=len(trn)

# ---------- 1. time-series CV of the non-parametric learners vs the linear model
def ts_cv(make, use_cols, target='lgy', min_train=40, h=4, step=2):
    errs=[];errs_lin=[]
    idx=trn.index.to_numpy()
    for k in range(min_train,len(idx)-h+1,step):
        tri=idx[:k]; tei=idx[k:k+h]
        Xtr=X.loc[tri,use_cols].values; Xte=X.loc[tei,use_cols].values
        ytr=trn.loc[tri,target].values; yte=trn.loc[tei,target].values
        m=make(); m.fit(Xtr,ytr)
        pr=m.predict(Xte)
        errs.extend(np.abs(np.exp(pr)-np.exp(yte)))
        # linear benchmark on the same split
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.column_stack([np.ones(len(tri)),Xtr]),ytr,rcond=None)[0]
        pl=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(tei)),Xte])@b
        errs_lin.extend(np.abs(np.exp(pl)-np.exp(yte)))
    return np.mean(errs), np.mean(errs_lin)

GB=lambda: GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=0,n_estimators=300,max_depth=2,learning_rate=0.03,loss='square_error')
RF=lambda: RandomForestRegressor(random_state=0,n_estimators=500,min_samples_leaf=3)
raw_cols=DR
log_cols=['log_'+c for c in DR]
print("time-series CV (expanding window, same folds):")
for name,mk,cols in [('GBM raw',GB,raw_cols),('GBM log',GB,log_cols),
                      ('RF raw',RF,raw_cols),('RF log',RF,log_cols)]:
    a,b=ts_cv(mk,cols)
    print(f"  {name:9s} MAE={a:.5f}   (in-fold OLS on same features: {b:.5f})")

# ---------- 2. what do the learners say drives the default rate?
m=GB(); m.fit(X.loc[trn.index,raw_cols].values, trn.lgy.values)
imp=pd.Series(m.feature_importances_,index=raw_cols).sort_values(ascending=False)
print("\nGBM feature importance (drop q37):")
print(imp.round(3).to_string())
# permutation importance on a held-out tail
te=trn[trn.quarter>65]; trn2=trn[trn.quarter<=65]
m2=GB(); m2.fit(X.loc[trn2.index,raw_cols].values, trn2.lgy.values)
base=np.mean((np.exp(m2.predict(X.loc[te.index,raw_cols].values))-te.default_rate.values)**2)
print("\npermutation importance (holdout q66-80, drop q37):")
rows=[]
for c in raw_cols:
    Xp=X.loc[te.index,raw_cols].copy()
    rng=np.random.default_rng(0); Xp[c]=rng.permutation(Xp[c].values)
    p=np.mean((np.exp(m2.predict(Xp.values))-te.default_rate.values)**2)
    rows.append((c,(p-base)/base))
for c,v in sorted(rows,key=lambda r:-r[1]): print(f"   {c:14s} {v:+.3f}")

# ---------- 3. scenario forecast from the non-parametric learners
print("\nscenario forecasts from non-parametric learners (drop q37):")
for name,mk,cols in [('GBM raw',GB,raw_cols),('GBM log',GB,log_cols),('RF log',RF,log_cols)]:
    m=mk(); m.fit(X.loc[trn.index,cols].values, trn.lgy.values)
    p=np.exp(m.predict(X.loc[scn.index,cols].values))
    print(f"  {name:9s} {p[0]:.4f} -> {p[-1]:.4f}   path: {np.round(p,4)}")
EOF

"""(a) Does the model reproduce the observed MAGNITUDE of spread-driven changes?
   (b) Are the forecast errors symmetric in logs, or should the band be asymmetric?"""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
tr=tr.copy(); trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)

# ---------- (a) magnitude check: observed vs model-implied quarter-to-quarter change
print("=" * 88)
print("(a) response-magnitude check: model-implied vs observed change in log(default rate)")
for spec_cols,lab in [(['bbb_spread'],'bbb only'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment'],'bbb+unemp'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],'bbb+unemp+vix')]:
    spec=dict(cols=spec_cols, log=tuple(c for c in spec_cols if c!='unemployment'))
    d=trn.dropna(subset=list(spec_cols)+['lgy'])
    X=B.design(d,spec); m=__import__('statsmodels.api',fromlist=['api']).OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
    fitted=np.asarray(m.fittedvalues); obs=d.lgy.values
    dobs=np.diff(obs); dfit=np.diff(fitted)
    sl=np.polyfit(dfit,dobs,1)[0]
    r=np.corrcoef(dfit,dobs)[0,1]
    print(f"  {lab:16s} n={len(dobs):3d}  slope(observed vs model-implied)={sl:.3f}  corr={r:.3f}")
# the two biggest observed spread-driven moves
d=trn.dropna(subset=['bbb_spread','lgy'])
q=d.quarter.values; b=d.bbb_spread.values; l=d.lgy.values
for a,bb in [(54,66),(57,65),(10,21),(43,55)]:
    if a in q and bb in q:
        ia=np.where(q==a)[0][0]; ib=np.where(q==bb)[0][0]
        print(f"  q{a}->q{bb}: bbb {b[ia]:.2f}->{b[ib]:.2f} (x{b[ib]/b[ia]:.2f})  "
              f"observed log-rate change {l[ib]-l[ia]:+.2f}  (x{np.exp(l[ib]-l[ia]):.2f})")

# ---------- (b) symmetry of the forecast error in logs
print("=" * 88)
print("(b) empirical distribution of backtest log-errors (log actual - log predicted)")
errs=[];rows=[]
for t in range(40,81):
    train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
    if len(tgt)==0: continue
    o=B.run_forecast(train,tgt,cv_stride=3)
    act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0]); yp=float(o['y_pred'][0])
    errs.append(np.log(act)-np.log(yp)); rows.append((t,act,yp))
e=np.array(errs)
print(f"  n={len(e)}  mean={e.mean():+.3f}  sd={e.std(ddof=1):.3f}  skew={pd.Series(e).skew():+.2f}")
print(f"  empirical 2.5% / 97.5% quantiles: {np.percentile(e,2.5):+.3f} / {np.percentile(e,97.5):+.3f}")
print(f"  normal  band at sigma=0.402      : {-1.96*0.402:+.3f} / {+1.96*0.402:+.3f}")
print(f"  -> asymmetry (upper-lower width ratio): {np.percentile(e,97.5)-np.percentile(e,2.5):.3f} vs {2*1.96*0.402:.3f}")
EOF

"""Does the model over-predict CHANGES?  Tested out-of-sample (the backtest model is
   always fit on past data only), so in-sample noise absorption cannot explain it."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
tr=tr.copy()

# ---------- A. out-of-sample: regress the backtest log-error on the predicted change
print("=" * 88)
print("A. out-of-sample damping test:  err_t = log(actual)-log(pred)  ~  predicted change_t")
rows=[]
for t in range(41,81):
    train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
    if len(tgt)==0: continue
    o=B.run_forecast(train,tgt,cv_stride=4)
    act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0]); yp=float(o['y_pred'][0])
    # predicted change: refit at t-1 to get the previous forecast
    if t-1<41: continue
    train2=tr[tr.quarter<t-1]; tgt2=tr[tr.quarter==t-1]
    o2=B.run_forecast(train2,tgt2,cv_stride=4)
    yp_prev=float(o2['y_pred'][0])
    rows.append((t,act,yp,yp_prev,float(o['sigma'][0])))
df=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=['q','act','pred','pred_prev','sigma'])
df['err']=np.log(df.act)-np.log(df.pred)
df['dhat']=np.log(df.pred)-np.log(df.pred_prev)
X=sm.add_constant(df[['dhat']])
m=sm.OLS(df.err.values,X).fit()
print(f"   n={len(df)}  slope on predicted change = {m.params[1]:+.3f} (t={m.tvalues[1]:+.2f})")
print(f"   mean error = {df.err.mean():+.3f} (t={df.err.mean()/(df.err.std(ddof=1)/np.sqrt(len(df))):+.2f})")
print(f"   corr(err, predicted change) = {np.corrcoef(df.err,df.dhat)[0,1]:+.3f}")

# ---------- B. in-sample change-attenuation, with and without a persistent component
print("=" * 88)
print("B. in-sample: observed vs model-implied quarter-to-quarter change, and the")
print("   persistence of the residuals (a persistent component would inflate bbb)")
trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)
def fitcols(cols, logc):
    spec=dict(cols=cols, log=logc)
    d=trn.dropna(subset=list(cols)+['lgy'])
    X=B.design(d,spec); m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
    return m,d
for cols,logc,lab in [(['bbb_spread'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb only'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb+unemp'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],('bbb_spread','vix'),'bbb+unemp+vix'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'],('bbb_spread','gdp'),'bbb+unemp+gdp'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment','nasdaq'],('bbb_spread','nasdaq'),'bbb+unemp+nasdaq')]:
    m,d=fitcols(cols,logc)
    res=np.asarray(m.resid); y=d.lgy.values
    r1=np.corrcoef(res[:-1],res[1:])[0,1]
    fitted=np.asarray(m.fittedvalues)
    slope=np.polyfit(np.diff(fitted),np.diff(y),1)[0]
    print(f"   {lab:20s} n={len(d):3d}  beta_bbb={m.params[1]:+.3f}  lag1 autocorr(resid)={r1:+.3f}  "
          f"change-attenuation slope={slope:.3f}")

# ---------- C. does adding a persistent (AR1) component change the bbb elasticity?
print("=" * 88)
print("C. bbb elasticity with an explicit AR(1) term in the target")
for cols,logc,lab in [(['bbb_spread'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb only'),
                       (['bbb_spread','unemployment'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb+unemp')]:
    d=trn.dropna(subset=list(cols)+['lgy']).copy()
    d['lgy_l1']=d.lgy.shift(1)
    d=d.dropna(subset=['lgy_l1'])
    spec=dict(cols=cols, log=logc)
    X=B.design(d,spec); X.insert(1,'lgy_l1',d.lgy_l1.values)
    m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
    co=" ".join(f"{c}:{m.params.values[i+1]:+.3f}(t{m.tvalues.values[i+1]:+.1f})"
                for i,c in enumerate(['AR1']+cols))
    print(f"   {lab:14s} n={len(d):3d} R2={m.rsquared:.3f} {co}")
EOF
timeout 1700 python work/attenuation.py
```

cd /workspace && cat > work/horizon.py <<'EOF'
"""The scenario is a 9-QUARTER path.  Two questions:
   (1) how does the estimated elasticity to log(bbb_spread) vary with the change
       horizon k?  (level regressions can be inflated by a persistent component)
   (2) can the model forecast the LEVEL h quarters ahead - the scenario's horizon -
       without systematic over-prediction of the change?
"""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)

# ---------- (1) elasticity vs change horizon
print("=" * 92)
print("(1) elasticity of log(default rate) to log(bbb_spread) by change horizon k")
d=trn.dropna(subset=['bbb_spread','unemployment','lgy']).copy()
for k in [1,2,3,4,6,8,12]:
    dd=d.copy()
    dd['dlgy']=dd.lgy-dd.lgy.shift(k); dd['dbbb']=np.log(dd.bbb_spread)-np.log(dd.bbb_spread).shift(k)
    dd['du']=dd.unemployment-dd.unemployment.shift(k)
    dd=dd.dropna(subset=['dlgy','dbbb','du'])
    if len(dd)<20: continue
    m1=sm.OLS(dd.dlgy.values, sm.add_constant(dd[['dbbb']])).fit()
    m2=sm.OLS(dd.dlgy.values, sm.add_constant(dd[['dbbb','du']])).fit()
    print(f"   k={k:2d}  n={len(dd):3d}  bbb elasticity (univariate) {m1.params.values[1]:+.3f} (t{m1.tvalues.values[1]:+.2f})"
          f"   | +unemployment: {m2.params.values[1]:+.3f} (t{m2.tvalues.values[1]:+.2f})")

# ---------- (2) multi-step level backtest
print("=" * 92)
print("(2) multi-step-ahead LEVEL backtest (fit on past only), scenario horizon = 4..9 q")
for h in [1,2,4,6,8]:
    errs=[];cov=[];slope_num=0;slope_den=0
    for t in range(30,81-h):
        train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter>=t]; tgt=tgt[tgt.quarter<t+h]
        if len(tgt)==0: continue
        try: o=B.run_forecast(train,tgt,cv_stride=4)
        except Exception: continue
        act=tgt.default_rate.values; pred=o['y_pred']
        errs.extend(np.abs(pred-act)); cov.extend((o['y_lower']<=act)&(act<=o['y_upper']))
        # does the predicted change over the block match the realised change?
        prev=B.run_forecast(train,tr[tr.quarter==t-1],cv_stride=4)['y_pred'][0] if t>31 else np.nan
        if np.isfinite(prev):
            dp=np.log(pred[-1])-np.log(prev); da=np.log(act[-1])-np.log(act[0])
            slope_num+=dp*da; slope_den+=dp*dp
    e=np.array(errs); c=np.array(cov)
    print(f"   h={h}: n={len(e):3d}  MAE={e.mean():.5f}  coverage={c.mean():.3f}  "
          f"realised-vs-predicted change slope={slope_num/slope_den if slope_den else np.nan:+.3f}")
EOF

cd /workspace && cat > work/damping.py <<'EOF'
"""Should the scenario path be damped?  Test empirically in the backtest:
   plain forecast  vs  forecast with the change-from-last-observation shrunk by d."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
for h in [4,8]:
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"multi-step backtest, h={h}")
    res={}
    for damp in [1.0,0.95,0.9,0.85,0.8]:
        errs=[];cov=[]
        for t in range(30,81-h):
            train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[(tr.quarter>=t)&(tr.quarter<t+h)]
            if len(tgt)==0: continue
            try: o=B.run_forecast(train,tgt,cv_stride=4)
            except Exception: continue
            last=float(train.default_rate.dropna().values[-1])   # last observed rate
            pred=o['y_pred']
            damped=last*(pred/last)**damp
            act=tgt.default_rate.values
            errs.extend(np.abs(damped-act))
            lo=last*(o['y_lower']/last)**damp; hi=last*(o['y_upper']/last)**damp
            cov.extend((lo<=act)&(act<=hi))
        e=np.array(errs); c=np.array(cov)
        print(f"   damp={damp:.2f}: MAE={e.mean():.5f}  RMSE={np.sqrt((e**2).mean()):.5f}  coverage={c.mean():.3f}")
        res[damp]=e.mean()
    best=min(res,key=res.get)
    print(f"   -> best damping factor: {best}")
EOF
timeout 1700 python work/damping.py
```

## What I tested

**A different model class.** Gradient boosting and random forests on identical rows and folds are *worse* than the parsimonious log-linear fit (CV MAE 0.0101–0.0107 vs 0.0085–0.0088) — at n≈70 with this noise, structure beats flexibility. Crucially, the learners independently **corroborate the driver ranking**: GBM permutation importance on a held-out tail gives bbb_spread +0.449 versus cpi +0.074, nasdaq +0.048, unemployment +0.044, gdp −0.078. Their flatter scenario path (×1.07–1.46) is a tree *extrapolation* artefact — trees cannot extrapolate a log-linear spread response — and both sit inside my reported band.

**A worry I had to chase down.** An in-sample diagnostic showed the model's quarter-to-quarter changes are ~half the size of the observed changes (slope 0.53), which would have meant the spread elasticity of 1.39 was inflated by a common trend. Two follow-ups resolved it:
- The multi-quarter elasticity — the one that matters for a 9-quarter path — is 1.16 (k=2), 1.19 (k=3), 1.24 (k=4), 0.91 (k=6), 0.80 (k=8), 0.98 (k=12), consistent with the level model.
- The multi-step level backtest at the scenario's horizon gives realised-vs-predicted change slopes of **+0.88 (h=4), +0.90 (h=6), +0.96 (h=8)** with MAE 0.0082–0.0086 and 97–99% coverage.

**Damping, tested rather than assumed.** Shrinking the path toward the last observed rate does *not* improve the multi-step MAE (0.00815 → 0.00818/0.00820/0.00825) and degrades coverage, so the undamped path stands.

**Band shape.** Backtest log-errors are near-symmetric (mean +0.077, skew +0.08) with empirical 2.5/97.5% quantiles of −0.54/+0.72 — *narrower* than my shipped band, so the interval is conservative, not inflated. I kept it symmetric because the identified downside risk (the "keep q37" treatment → 0.033 at q89) must stay covered.

One correction along the way: my first cut of the orthogonality argument for that 0.53 slope was wrong — OLS makes the residual *vector* orthogonal to the column space, not each fitted value pointwise — which is why the diagnostic needed the out-of-sample test rather than an algebraic claim.

"""Is the noise multiplicative (log-normal) or additive in levels?  This decides the
   SHAPE of the prediction band: proportional (y*[a,b]) vs constant-width (y+-c)."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
tr=tr.copy(); trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)

# ---------- 1. homoskedasticity: does the residual scale grow with the fitted level?
print("=" * 92)
print("1. residual scale vs fitted level (log-target model, bbb+unemp+trend, n=70)")
spec=dict(cols=['bbb_spread','unemployment'], log=('bbb_spread',), trend=True)
d=trn.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['lgy'])
X=B.design(d,spec); m=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
fit=np.asarray(m.fittedvalues); res=np.asarray(m.resid); y=d.lgy.values
q=pd.qcut(fit,4,labels=['low','mid-low','mid-high','high'])
df=pd.DataFrame({'fit':fit,'res':res,'y':y,'bin':q})
print(df.groupby('bin',observed=True).apply(lambda g: pd.Series({
    'n':len(g),
    'mean_fitted_level':np.exp(g.fit.mean()),
    'sd_log_resid':g.res.std(ddof=1),
    'sd_level_resid':(np.exp(g.fit+g.res)-np.exp(g.fit)).std(ddof=1),
    'cv_level':(np.exp(g.fit+g.res)-np.exp(g.fit)).std(ddof=1)/np.exp(g.fit).mean(),
}),include_groups=False).round(4).to_string())
# correlation of |resid| with fitted level (log-target) and of |level resid| with level
absres=np.abs(res); lvlres=np.abs(np.exp(fit+res)-np.exp(fit))
print(f"\n   corr(|log resid|, fitted log level)   = {np.corrcoef(absres,fit)[0,1]:+.3f}   "
      f"(0 => homoskedastic in logs)")
print(f"   corr(|level resid|, fitted level)      = {np.corrcoef(lvlres,np.exp(fit))[0,1]:+.3f}   "
      f"(0 => homoskedastic in levels)")

# ---------- 2. backtest: log-target ensemble vs level-target ensemble
print("=" * 92)
print("2. backtest: log-target vs level-target ensemble (point-forecast accuracy)")
import build_predictions as BP
# level-target variant of the production machinery
orig_fit_member = BP.fit_member
def fit_member_level(train_df, target_df, spec, treatment):
    df=train_df.copy()
    if treatment=='drop': df=df[df.quarter!=37]
    d=df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['default_rate'])
    if len(d)<20 or target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any(): return None
    X=BP.design(d,spec)
    m=sm.OLS(d.default_rate.values,X).fit()
    resid=np.asarray(m.resid); sd=float(np.std(resid,ddof=X.shape[1]))
    mse=float(resid@resid/max(len(d)-X.shape[1],1))
    Xs=BP.design(target_df,spec)[X.columns]
    p=np.asarray(m.predict(Xs))
    inv=np.linalg.pinv(X.values.T@X.values)
    lev=np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i',Xs.values,inv,Xs.values)
    return dict(spec=spec,treatment=treatment,m=m,d=d,X=X,sd=sd,se=mse*np.sqrt(lev),p=p,n=len(d))
def run_level(train_df,target_df):
    mem=[]
    for t in BP.TREATMENTS:
        for spec in BP.MODELS:
            f=fit_member_level(train_df,target_df,spec,t)
            if f is None: continue
            f['cv']=BP.cv_score(train_df,spec,t,stride=4) if False else np.nan
            mem.append(f)
    # weight by the same CV as the log-target members (apples to apples)
    cvs=[]
    for t in BP.TREATMENTS:
        for spec in BP.MODELS:
            d=train_df.copy()
            if t=='drop': d=d[d.quarter!=37]
            dd=d.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['default_rate'])
            if len(dd)<20: cvs.append(np.nan); continue
            errs=[]
            for tt in range(int(dd.quarter.min())+20,int(dd.quarter.max())-3,3):
                a=dd[dd.quarter<tt]; b2=dd[(dd.quarter>=tt)&(dd.quarter<tt+4)]
                if len(a)<15 or len(b2)==0: continue
                bb=np.linalg.lstsq(BP.design(a,spec).values,a.default_rate.values,rcond=None)[0]
                pr=BP.design(b2,spec).values@bb
                errs.extend(np.abs(pr-b2.default_rate.values))
            cvs.append(np.mean(errs) if errs else np.nan)
    cvs=np.array(cvs); ok=np.isfinite(cvs)
    expo=np.where(ok,-(cvs-np.nanmin(cvs[ok]))/BP.TAU,0.0); w=np.exp(expo); w=w/w.sum()
    P=np.array([f['p'] for f in mem])
    return (w[:,None]*P).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()

for lab,fn in [('log target  (production)', lambda a,b: B.run_forecast(a,b,cv_stride=4)['y_pred']),
               ('level target', run_level)]:
    errs=[];lerrs=[]
    for t in range(40,81):
        train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
        if len(tgt)==0: continue
        try: pred=fn(train,tgt)
        except Exception: continue
        act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0])
        errs.append(abs(pred[0]-act)); lerrs.append(abs(np.log(act)-np.log(pred[0])))
    e=np.array(errs); le=np.array(lerrs)
    print(f"   {lab:24s} MAE(level)={e.mean():.5f}  RMSE(level)={np.sqrt((e**2).mean()):.5f}  "
          f"MAE(log)={le.mean():.4f}  bias(log)={np.mean(-le):+.3f}")

"""Controlled comparison of the target link (log vs level) on identical rows, folds
   and ensemble weights - the link is the other structural choice I cannot resolve
   from the data, so it may need marginalising over too."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
import build_predictions as B

comb, tr, sc, scraw = B.load_data()
tr=tr.copy(); trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].reset_index(drop=True)

print("=" * 92)
print("1. in-sample fit on identical rows (n=70, q10-80 excl q37)")
for cols,logc,lab in [(['bbb_spread','unemployment'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb+unemp'),
                      (['bbb_spread','unemployment','vix'],('bbb_spread','vix'),'bbb+unemp+vix'),
                      (['bbb_spread','unemployment','gdp'],('bbb_spread','gdp'),'bbb+unemp+gdp'),
                      (['bbb_spread','unemployment','nasdaq'],('bbb_spread','nasdaq'),'bbb+unemp+nasdaq'),
                      (['bbb_spread','unemployment'],('bbb_spread',),'bbb+unemp (trend)')]:
    spec=dict(cols=cols,log=logc,trend=(lab.endswith('(trend)'))
    d=trn.dropna(subset=list(cols)+['lgy'])
    X=B.design(d,spec)
    ml=sm.OLS(d.lgy.values,X).fit()
    mlev=sm.OLS(d.default_rate.values,X).fit()
    # level-model in-sample sd relative to the mean level
    cv=mlev.mse_resid**0.5/d.default_rate.mean()
    print(f"   {lab:20s} n={len(d):3d} | log: AIC={ml.aic:6.2f} sd_log={np.std(ml.resid,ddof=2):.3f}"
          f" | level: AIC={mlev.aic:6.2f} sd_lvl={mlev.mse_resid**0.5:.5f} (CV={cv:.3f})")

print("=" * 92)
print("2. controlled backtest (identical folds, identical ensemble weights)")
# production log-link members and their CV weights
def log_members(train_df,target_df,stride=4):
    mem=[];cvs=[]
    for t in B.TREATMENTS:
        for spec in B.MODELS:
            f=B.fit_member(train_df,target_df,spec,t)
            if f is None: continue
            f['cv']=B.cv_score(train_df,spec,t,stride=stride)
            mem.append(f); cvs.append(f['cv'])
    cvs=np.array(cvs); ok=np.isfinite(cvs)
    expo=np.where(ok,-(cvs-np.nanmin(cvs[ok]))/B.TAU,0.0); w=np.exp(expo); w=w/w.sum()
    return mem,w
def level_members(train_df,target_df,w):
    out=[]
    for t in B.TREATMENTS:
        for spec in B.MODELS:
            df=train_df.copy()
            if t=='drop': df=df[df.quarter!=37]
            d=df.dropna(subset=list(spec['cols'])+['default_rate'])
            if len(d)<20 or target_df[list(spec['cols'])].isna().values.any():
                out.append(None); continue
            X=B.design(d,spec); m=sm.OLS(d.default_rate.values,X).fit()
            Xs=B.design(target_df,spec)[X.columns]
            out.append(np.asarray(m.predict(Xs)))
    return out

res={'log':[], 'level':[], 'combo':[]}
for t in range(40,81):
    train=tr[tr.quarter<t]; tgt=tr[tr.quarter==t]
    if len(tgt)==0: continue
    mem,w=log_members(train,tgt)
    P_log=np.array([f['p'] for f in mem])            # log scale
    pl=(w[:,None]*np.exp(P_log)).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()
    PL=level_members(train,tgt,w)
    okl=[i for i,p in enumerate(PL) if p is not None]
    plev=np.array([PL[i] for i in okl]); wl=w[okl]/w[okl].sum()
    ph=(wl[:,None]*plev).sum(axis=0)/wl.sum()
    pc=(w[:,None]*np.exp(P_log)).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()*0.5 + ph*0.5
    act=float(tgt.default_rate.values[0])
    res['log'].append((pl[0],act)); res['level'].append((ph[0],act)); res['combo'].append((pc[0],act))
for k,v in res.items():
    p=np.array([a for a,_ in v]); a=np.array([b for _,b in v])
    print(f"   {k:6s}: MAE(level)={np.mean(np.abs(p-a)):.5f}  RMSE={np.sqrt(np.mean((p-a)**2)):.5f}  "
          f"MAE(log)={np.mean(np.abs(np.log(p)-np.log(a))):.4f}  "
          f"mean signed log err={np.mean(np.log(a)-np.log(p)):+.3f}")
print("=" * 92)

A linear-in-level response is therefore sub-proportional where the true one is proportional.

"""Assumption-light cross-check: for every scenario quarter, find the historical
   quarters whose driver configuration is most similar and look at what the
   default rate actually did there.  No regression is involved."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist

tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
DR=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']
trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].copy()            # the anomaly row is not an analogue

# standardise drivers on the training sample (log for the positive series)
mu=trn[DR].apply(np.log).mean(); sd=trn[DR].apply(np.log).std()
Ztr=np.log(trn[DR]); Ztr=(Ztr-mu)/sd
Zsc=(np.log(sc[DR])-mu)/sd

print("=" * 96)
print("nearest-neighbour analogues in driver space (standardised log drivers)")
pred=pd.read_csv('predictions.csv').set_index('quarter')
for k in [3,5,8]:
    print(f"\n--- k={k} nearest training quarters per scenario quarter")
    for i,q in enumerate(sc.quarter):
        d=cdist(Zsc.iloc[[i]].values,Ztr.values)[0]
        order=np.argsort(d)[:k]
        near=trn.iloc[order]
        # also the closest single quarter
        j=order[0]
        print(f"  q{q}: nearest q{int(near.quarter.iloc[0])} "
              f"(d={d[order[0]]:.2f}) | mean rate of {k} nearest = {near.default_rate.mean():.4f} "
              f"| model says {pred.loc[q,'y_pred']:.4f} "
              f"[{pred.loc[q,'y_lower']:.4f},{pred.loc[q,'y_upper']:.4f}]")
    # summary
    rows=[]
    for i,q in enumerate(sc.quarter):
        d=cdist(Zsc.iloc[[i]].values,Ztr.values)[0]
        near=trn.iloc[np.argsort(d)[:k]]
        rows.append((q,near.default_rate.mean(),pred.loc[q,'y_pred']))
    df=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=['q','analogue','model'])
    print(f"  => mean analogue rate {df.analogue.mean():.4f} vs mean model {df.model.mean():.4f}"
          f"   (analogue inside model band for {int(((df.analogue>=pred.y_lower.reindex(df.q).values)&(df.analogue<=pred.y_upper.reindex(df.q).values)).sum())}/{len(df)} quarters)")
EOF
timeout 600 python work/analogues.py
```

"""Is the scenario inside the joint support of the training drivers?  (Mahalanobis
   distance in the standardised driver space, and the leverage of the fitted models)"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
DR=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']
trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].copy()
mu=trn[DR].apply(np.log).mean(); sd=trn[DR].apply(np.log).std()
Ztr=((np.log(trn[DR])-mu)/sd).values
Zsc=((np.log(sc[DR])-mu)/sd).values

# distances: scenario -> training, and training -> training (for reference)
d_sc_tr=cdist(Zsc,Ztr)
D=np.sqrt(((Ztr[:,None,:]-Ztr[None,:,:])**2).sum(-1))
off=D[np.triu_indices(len(Ztr),1)]
print("Euclidean distance in standardised log-driver space")
print(f"  training-to-training: median {np.median(off):.2f}  p90 {np.percentile(off,90):.2f}  max {off.max():.2f}")
for i,q in enumerate(sc.quarter):
    print(f"  scenario q{q}: nearest training distance {d_sc_tr[i].min():.2f}  "
          f"(rank of this distance within the training-to-training distribution: "
          f"{100*(off<d_sc_tr[i].min()).mean():.0f}th pct)")

# Mahalanobis distance in the driver space (using the training covariance)
cov=np.cov(Ztr.T); P=np.linalg.pinv(cov)
def maha(A,B):
    d=A[:,None,:]-B[None,:,:]
    return np.sqrt(np.einsum('ijk,kl,ijl->ij',d,P,d))
M_sc_tr=maha(Zsc,Ztr)
M_tr=np.sqrt(np.einsum('ijk,kl,ijl->ij',(Ztr[:,None,:]-Ztr[None,:,:]),P,(Ztr[:,None,:]-Ztr[None,:,:])))
offM=M_tr[np.triu_indices(len(Ztr),1)]
print(f"\nMahalanobis distance")
print(f"  training-to-training: median {np.median(offM):.2f}  p90 {np.percentile(offM,90):.2f}  max {offM.max():.2f}")
for i,q in enumerate(sc.quarter):
    j=M_sc_tr[i].argmin()
    print(f"  scenario q{q}: nearest training q{int(trn.quarter.iloc[j])} at Mahalanobis {M_sc_tr[i,j]:.2f} "
          f"-> {100*(offM<M_sc_tr[i,j]).mean():.0f}th pct of training-to-training distances")
EOF
timeout 600 python work/support_check.py
```

import numpy as np, pandas as pd

trn=tr[tr.quarter!=37].dropna(subset=DR).copy()
mu=trn[DR].apply(np.log).mean(); sd=trn[DR].apply(np.log).std()
Ztr=((np.log(trn[DR])-mu)/sd).values; Zsc=((np.log(sc[DR])-mu)/sd).values
C=np.cov(Ztr.T); w,V=np.linalg.eigh(C); order=np.argsort(w)[::-1]; w=w[order]; V=V[:,order]
print("covariance eigenvalues:", np.round(w,3))
